fatal_flaws.claim: Sec.3 workhorse and loop: 'ΔV_k = E[(1−π)/π]·I_k' from Kallus–Mao / PPI; the rubric is a cheap channel that stands in for the expensive outcome ('low-rank fast evaluation').
fatal_flaws.problem: PPI, Kallus–Mao and active labelling all assume the surrogate is cheap and the label is expensive. On AppWorld it is the other way round. Y (won, G) comes free from programmatic goal checks once a trajectory exists; the cost is generating the trajectory, and every rubric score also needs that trajectory. So Y is never missing where S is observed, and by the framework's own P1(i) ΔV=0 there. The only missingness is at the candidate level: some candidates get no Validation run. The units are therefore ~36 candidates (~11 gold at π=0.3), not thousands of labels. The whole apparatus reduces to predicting Validation lift from ~25 Discovery features across 36 candidates. That is a small-n regression PPI cannot help, and it saves no cost per trajectory.
fatal_flaws.fix: Say plainly that the estimation value exists only for skipped Validation runs and sealed or new families (a transport or prediction problem). Make the primary value of a rubric dimension its value for design and direction (see below), not its value as a label surrogate. Alternatively, move missingness to the (candidate, task) cell: use task-level Horvitz–Thompson sampling of Validation tasks, so the units number in the hundreds.

fatal_flaws.claim: G1 (week 8): 'V_{Y-only}/V_R ≥ 1.5; kill the approach if V_{Y-only}/V_R < 1.2'.
fatal_flaws.problem: There is a hard ceiling. Gold is one 50-task Validation pass, with paired SE σ_e≈0.06 from the empirical check, and π=0.3. Any Discovery-based h leaves σ_e² unexplained. So V_const/V_best = (σ_L²+σ_e²)(1+odds)/(σ_L²+σ_e²+odds·σ_e²). That is 1.16 at σ_L=3pp, 1.28 at 4pp and 1.40 at 5pp, even for a PERFECT predictor of the latent lift. With decent Discovery-to-Validation transfer, V_{Y-only}/V_best is only about 1.11–1.17 (numeric check). For natural candidates (true effects 1–7pp), 1.5 cannot be reached and the kill line of 1.2 sits at the ceiling. The gate kills the method even if the method works perfectly, and only planted degradations (σ_L≈16pp) could pass it.
fatal_flaws.fix: Pre-compute the ceiling. State G1 as the fraction of attainable reduction, (V_Y−V_R)/(V_Y−V_best) ≥ 0.4. Alternatively, lower σ_e with 2–3 Validation seeds on gold candidates, or target the posterior variance of the latent L_c. Report planted and natural candidates separately.

fatal_flaws.claim: Thesis: 'A wrong rubric therefore costs precision, never bias'; P2 'ψ̂^DR is unbiased for any index h'; worked example 'effective-sample multiplier ≈1.44'.
fatal_flaws.problem: (a) Design-unbiasedness holds for averages over candidates, such as the mean lift of an arm's proposals. It does not hold for a single candidate. An un-golded candidate's estimate is h(Z_c), which is fully model-based. A golded one is h + (1/π)(L̂−h), with weights up to 10×. Promotion already requires gold, so the rubric adds no precision to the promote decision. (b) The 1.44 multiplier comes from a cross-candidate restriction (q invariant) and contradicts P1(i), because Y is observed on every Discovery run. That restriction is violated by exactly the existing strip-answer candidates, which change q rather than p. So the flagship example is a biased model-based gain. (c) In a self-evolving loop, the real cost of a hacked rubric is search regret (wasted proposals and gold), and that is not bias. 'Goodhart-safe' overclaims.
fatal_flaws.fix: State the guarantee's scope: design-unbiased arm- or proposer-level functionals; per-candidate posteriors carry explicit model risk. Drop the 1.44 example or label it model-based and conditional on an audited q-invariance. Rename P2 'Goodhart-safe inference', and add a regret statement or leave optimisation safety as an explicit limitation.

fatal_flaws.claim: Loop: 'Discovery: live tasks first (Neyman n_t ∝ sd_t; deterministic tasks reused)'.
fatal_flaws.problem: About 2/3 of tasks are deterministic under the INCUMBENT, and most of them are deterministic failures from budget exhaustion (75–88% of failures). Those are exactly the tasks an improving edit must flip. Reusing incumbent outcomes there imputes zero effect, and sd_t is the null standard deviation, so Neyman gives them zero weight. Lift estimates are biased toward 0 for real improvements, while noise on live tasks drives decisions. The '≈3× saving' is bought with bias.
fatal_flaws.fix: Sample deterministic tasks with a known π_t>0 and use Horvitz–Thompson weighting. Allocate by the standard deviation of the paired difference under the alternative. Use hook-activation logs: tasks on which the edit's trigger provably cannot fire can be down-weighted, but still sampled at a small known rate because runs are not seed-reproducible.

fatal_flaws.claim: Setup: Θ* Tucker with 'r₃ ≤ 5 capability factors (Planning…Verification)'; deficit target Γ_{f,j}; '(f,j) ← argmax LCB(deficit)'; 'moving from general ability to an edge case only changes w_V'.
fatal_flaws.problem: (a) Tucker factors are identified only up to rotation, so 'capability j' is not a coordinate of Θ*, and ⟨Γ_{f,j},Θ*⟩ is not identified. (b) Pairing removes β_t only for contrasts. The deficit is a LEVEL for c*, and Θ_{c*,f,k} is confounded with the family-level part of β_{t,k}: hard families look deficient whatever the harness can do. (c) Validation families are new, so they have no family-mode observations outside gold. (d) A single-family Γ has V_eff about F times larger, so edge-case deficits are the least estimable quantity at 50 tasks. Statistical 'localization from general to edge case' is therefore undefined, and at this budget also unestimable.
fatal_flaws.fix: Anchor capabilities with a confirmatory structure: pre-assign programmatic channels to capability groups and fix those loadings. Define the deficit as an identified contrast, such as headroom versus a reference or oracle harness or the best candidate on (f, group), or the rate of mechanism-trigger firing conditional on failure. Localize edge cases by mechanism triggers plus generated tasks (Self-Challenging / AutoBencher-style), not by family-level estimation.

fatal_flaws.claim: Admission via α-investing on t_k with 36 candidates; G2 'Spearman(Î_k half A, realized I_k half B) ≥ 0.4 over ≥20 dimensions'; mitigation 'pooling the ALFWorld logs'.
fatal_flaws.problem: At n=36, the detectable OBSERVED partial r (80% power) is 0.46 at α=.05 and 0.57 at α=.005. Reliability of L̂ is about 0.2–0.4 for σ_L 3–5pp, so the latent partial correlation must be about 0.8 or more. LLM-proposed atomic checks will essentially never be admitted; only completion or steps will, and only if planted degradations dominate Var(L). I simulated G2 with 18 candidates per half and generous true correlations (0–0.6). The mean split-half Spearman was 0.02–0.12, and P(≥0.4) was under 10%. The empirical check also found no ALFWorld per-game results, so the pooling mitigation does not exist.
fatal_flaws.fix: Pre-register a power analysis. Raise breadth by using (candidate × family) or (candidate × task) contrasts with a hierarchical or low-rank model. Calibrate G2's threshold by simulation, or replace it with a check of predicted versus realized variance reduction on planted-plus-natural candidates. Use planted candidates only for calibration and never for admission. Drop the ALFWorld pooling claim.

fatal_flaws.claim: Explanation of the past failure: 'Generic dimensions load on the general factor … ⟨u,H_D⟩≈0. This is a formal account of why rubric v1/v2 failed'; TC 'becomes a separate gate on direction'; G3 is secondary.
fatal_flaws.problem: rubric_abc stalled because its dimensions induced DEAD-HOOK proposals. That is a failure of direction and actionability (TC≈0), not of measurement. ΔV_k cannot detect or prevent it. The user asked for a rubric that localizes gaps and actively drives capability gains, but the only mathematical content here is about measurement. The direction value is tested only by G3, which cannot fail in a meaningful way. Promotion needs a winner's-curse-corrected LCB>0 with σ_e≈6pp, so almost nothing is promoted and the arms tie. The sealed test at 3 seeds has an MDE of about 10pp against arm differences of a few pp. 'Ties while using ≥30% fewer passes' then passes vacuously. The paper's claim about self-evolution has no power behind it.
fatal_flaws.fix: Make direction value the headline and give it its own mathematics. A dimension's value is the expected paired gain of the proposals it induces, estimated as metaproductivity / knowledge gradient with Beta or Gaussian Thompson sampling over diagnosed mechanisms. Evaluate each induced proposal on its mechanism's trigger set, where the effect is concentrated: if the effect lives on a fraction s of tasks, the required paired n shrinks by about s. Include a small IPW sample of non-trigger tasks to bound harm. This turns 'localization' into a measurable power gain and ties it to the fast-evaluation story.

fatal_flaws.claim: Contribution claims P1–P3 plus the 'Nearest competitor' differentiation.
fatal_flaws.problem: P1 is the Schur complement / Zellner SUR / Kallus–Mao Cor. 2.1. P2 is AIPW/PPI++ with known propensities (Robins–Rotnitzky–Zhao, Zrnic–Candès). P3 is the Gaussian selection identity E[L|argmax h]. The admission rule is AlphaGen's increment-IC, Tripuraneni et al.'s proxy Sharpe, Barillas–Shanken and Feng–Giglio–Xiu. Yazdani et al. (2609.35646) already does Fisher-adaptive rubric criteria. The low-rank tensor, which is the user's distinctive asset, is never used in the estimator the paper actually computes (the linear-Gaussian workhorse is candidate-level). An ICML AC will read this as known statistics relabelled, on an empirical base of about 36 candidates with a probable null.
fatal_flaws.fix: Anchor novelty in something the literature lacks and the user can prove. Candidates: (i) an efficiency bound for a low-rank candidate × family effect tensor with post-treatment auxiliary channels and candidate-level missingness, where corollary (i) gives exactly when shared low rank creates value; (ii) a bound on the drift of surrogate value once the proposer optimises against h. Otherwise, position the paper as an empirical systems paper and keep P1–P3 as a short, correct lemma section.

math_errors: 'ΔV_k = E[(1−π)/π]·I_k' factorizes only when π is constant or independent of the residual variance. The loop sets π_c ∝ sd(L|Z_c)·P(L_c>0|Z_c)/√cost, which depends on Z and therefore on the rubric itself. The correct increment is E[odds(Z)Var(L|Z_D)] − E[odds'(Z)Var(L|Z_D,Z_k)], with π changing when k is added. Kallus–Mao also let labelling depend on X only; labelling on S is two-phase sampling, which has a different bound.

'I_k does not depend on the design' is misleading. I_k = σ_L²(1−R²_D)ρ²_{Lk·D} is a functional of the candidate-generating distribution, which the proposer changes every round and which planted candidates inflate. It is independent of π only.

P3: 'e_n ≈ √(2 log n)' overstates the exact expected maximum of n iid N(0,1) by 50–110% in the relevant range: n=3: 0.85 vs 1.48; n=5: 1.16 vs 1.79; n=8: 1.42 vs 2.04. P3 also needs independent proposals; equicorrelated proposals that share edits scale the gain by √(1−ρ₀). And it assumes constant π, which contradicts the loop's adaptive π.
P2 variance 'V_gold − odds·(2Cov(L,h) − Var h)' holds only against the centered (Hájek) gold estimator and for a mean-calibrated h (E h = E L). In general the reduction is odds·(2E[Lh] − E[h²]).

The worked example's 1.44 = (1−pq)/(q(1−p)) is arithmetically correct but contradicts P1(i): Y is observed on every Discovery run, so the DR gain is 0. The 1.44 exists only under the model restriction 'q invariant across candidates'.

'pairwise judge … only on TIED tasks (Y has ~0 Fisher info)': Fisher information is a property of the model at the parameter, not of realized outcomes. Choosing judge cells by an observed tie is outcome-dependent sampling. It is valid only as a two-phase design with a known selection rule, and the resulting win-rate channel depends on the candidate's effect.

Winner's curse is misapplied. Candidates are selected on h(Z_c) from Discovery and inferred from independent Validation gold, so L̂_c has no selection bias, and the AKM hybrid CIs needlessly lose power. The real problems are multiplicity across rounds and repeated reuse of Validation for fitting h, admission, audits and promotion, which overfits Validation adaptively.

Admission condition 2, ρ²_partial ≥ κ = judge cost / run cost, is not cost parity. Parity is ΔV_k/V_D ≥ κ/(1+κ), relative variance reduction against relative cost increase. It is also vacuous: κ≈0 for programmatic checks and ≈0.01 for judge items.
'Greedy admission by Î/cost is (1−e^{−γ})-optimal': the Das–Kempe bound is for cardinality constraints. Cost-weighted greedy under a budget needs partial enumeration or carries a weaker constant.

Martingale CLT under adaptive π_c and a refit h needs conditional-variance stabilization plus Lindeberg conditions (cf. Hadad et al. 2021). At n_gold≈11 asymptotic normality is not credible. Use randomization or permutation inference, or anytime-valid (betting) confidence sets.
A jackknife clustered by lineage with about 3–6 lineages is anti-conservative (few-cluster problem). Use a wild cluster bootstrap or t with G−1 degrees of freedom.

The information form ⟨G_D U,W⟩ = E[d_Dᵀ Σ_DD⁻¹ d_D] is Chamberlain's bound for the conditional-mean-restriction model. Mixing Bernoulli graded channels with BTL judge channels under an assumed joint likelihood gives a different bound, so the model must be stated.

Tucker capability factor j is rotation-unidentified, so Γ_{f,j} is not a well-defined linear functional of Θ*. Levels Θ_{c*,f,k} are confounded with the family component of β_{t,k}, and only cross-candidate contrasts are identified.

Audit 'the test of E[L−h(Z)] = 0 does not reject' accepts on absence of evidence with about 11–36 gold candidates. It needs an equivalence (TOST) bound. 'DR coverage ≥90% on planted effects' with 6 planted candidates cannot be tested: 6/6 gives a Clopper–Pearson CI of [0.54, 1].
strongest_ideas_to_keep: Noise coupling and innovation. If S = Y + noise, then ν_k = 0 and S is worthless even at ρ≈0.8 same-run correlation. A dimension's value is its partial alignment with the target direction, given as a⟨u,H⟩²/(1+a⟨u,A⁻¹u⟩) (Sherman–Morrison, verified correct), equivalently residual α²/σ²(ε) or the Gaussian conditional MI (partial IC). This is correct, simple, and speaks directly to the user's question of how to quantify whether a new reward dimension helps. Present it as a lemma plus a scorecard of alignment, dispersion and reliability, computed offline at zero GPU cost.

The 'credit feasibility calculator': compute V_eff(Γ_edit)/n in advance to see whether a component-credit question can be answered at the budget. It answers the user's credit-assignment frustration without per-token credit and agrees with POSTMORTEM_LOOP1 (every-step components are unanswerable, trigger components are answerable).

Keep the two roles of the rubric separate: measurement (surrogate) and direction (localization and proposals), with TC and downstream proposal gain against a token-matched control as the gate on direction. Promote direction to the primary target.
Design-based gold randomization with known π. This gives unbiased arm- or proposer-level lift even when h is hacked; the scope must be stated correctly.

The IC translation, stated honestly: IC buys blocking on the task factor, robustness to G's all-or-nothing jumps, and a focus on ordering, not extra power. Rank or sign tests on paired G were empirically better (power 0.89 vs 0.71 on the planted effect) and should be the default test.
Point the rubric at the binding constraint: budget exhaustion causes 75–88% of failures. Put a parse-fallback indicator into D so no dimension is credited for the default-code confound.

Trigger-set-targeted evaluation as the natural bridge between 'localize' and 'fast evaluation'. A mechanism-level dimension with a programmatic trigger concentrates each induced edit's effect on a fraction s of tasks. c-optimal allocation to that set, with a small IPW sample elsewhere, cuts the required n by about s. That makes the localization value of a dimension quantifiable.
Score new dimensions offline on all logged trajectories, and use α-investing over every dimension ever proposed.
overlap_with_prior_work: Kallus & Mao (JRSSB 2025) Cor. 2.1: the workhorse ΔV_k identity is a direct restatement. Zellner SUR covers corollary P1(i).
PPI / PPI++ (Angelopoulos et al. 2023), active inference (Zrnic & Candès ICML 2024), AM-PPI (2605.08429) and Robins–Rotnitzky–Zhao AIPW cover P2 and the gold-allocation rule.
Tripuraneni et al. KDD 2024 (proxy quality = alignment × SNR, Sharpe-optimal composite) and Jeunen & Ustimenko KDD 2024 (learned metrics) cover the cross-candidate IC and composite-weight idea.

Bibaut et al. KDD 2024 on weak-experiment covariance bias: the framework's claim that disjoint tasks remove it is fine for covariance but ignores time or load-correlated noise, since the 900 s timeouts on a shared box are shared across splits.

Yazdani et al. 'Rubric Rewards from IRT' (2609.35646, posted 2 days ago): Fisher-adaptive criterion selection over rubric verdicts. It is the nearest competitor, and c-optimal targeting alone is a thin separation.

Auto-Rubric (2510.17314, log-det / D-optimal), RLER/DR Tulu (std retention), OnlineRubrics (pairwise-contrast elicitation), VibeCheck (reliability × dispersion × alignment), CURE (reward precision μ>0): the admission scorecard overlaps with these.

AlphaGen (increment-IC reward for new alphas), R&D-Agent(Q), Feng–Giglio–Xiu double selection, Barillas–Shanken spanning: the 'value of a new factor given existing ones' template is established in quant.

Athey–Chetty–Imbens–Kang surrogate index, Prentice, and Chen–Geng–Jia / VanderWeele surrogate paradox: the audit layer. Landesberg & Narayan (2512.11150): oracle-slice calibration plus a transport audit is the same Goodhart-safe-inference design.
HGM (clade metaproductivity with Thompson sampling) and DGM objective hacking: the direction role and value by metaproductivity are already there for fixed evaluators.
Razin et al. NeurIPS 2025 and PAV (Setlur et al.): policy-dependent reward value and the distinguishability/alignment decomposition anticipate the retirement and drift discussion.
verdict: This is not publishable as designed. The core identities are correct. The worked-example arithmetic (1.44) is correct, the Sherman–Morrison increment is correct, and the S = Y + noise ⇒ ν = 0 insight is correct and useful. But the framework puts the rubric's value in the wrong place for this environment. On AppWorld the label Y is free once a trajectory exists, and every rubric score needs that same trajectory. So the PPI and Kallus–Mao estimation value exists only when whole Validation runs are skipped. That makes the units about 36 candidates, and the pre-registered gates are then close to unreachable. G1 has an analytic ceiling of about 1.16–1.4 even for a perfect predictor of natural-candidate lifts, against a 1.5 target and a 1.2 kill line. G2 passes with probability under 10% in simulation. The live loop promotes almost nothing because σ_e≈6pp, so G3 passes vacuously. The deficit map the user most cares about ('localize where abilities are lacking, general → edge case') is not identified: Tucker rotation, a level confounded with family difficulty, and new Validation families. Reusing deterministic tasks biases lifts toward zero on exactly the budget-exhaustion failures that edits must fix. On novelty, P1–P3 are known results (Kallus–Mao/SUR, AIPW/PPI, Gaussian selection), Yazdani et al. just posted Fisher-adaptive rubric criteria, and the user's low-rank machinery is decorative in the estimator actually computed. The minimal pivot keeps the good mathematics but moves the target from measurement to direction. First, value a mechanism-level dimension by the expected paired gain of the proposals it induces (metaproductivity / knowledge gradient, with a Thompson bandit over diagnosed mechanisms). Second, evaluate each induced edit on its trigger set with c-optimal allocation, which yields a power gain of about s; that is the quantified value of localization, and it is where 'fast evaluation' actually comes from. Third, keep the innovation/partial-IC scorecard as a zero-GPU screening lemma, rank and sign paired-G tests as the default IC translation, and design-randomized gold for arm-level unbiasedness with its scope stated correctly. Fourth, reserve the tensor efficiency theory for one genuinely new result: when shared low rank across channels makes a post-treatment dimension informative despite P1(i). Also pre-register power and ceiling calculations, fix the IPW on deterministic tasks, and drop the claims about ALFWorld pooling and the winner's curse.
